@AGENTS.md

# BrightPath — Framer → Next.js

A Next.js 16 (App Router) app that renders a Framer site through
[unframer](https://github.com/remorses/unframer). The design lives in Framer;
this repo consumes it as generated React components and supplies routing, CMS
data and a few behaviours the export cannot provide on its own.

Ported from the Vite version at `/home/lobster/Documents/example-unframer-app`.
Everything below that is not Next-specific applies to both.

**Nothing in `framer/` is hand-written.** It is regenerated by `pnpm framer`.
Every fix belongs in the files listed under "What we own", or in Framer itself.

```bash
npx @framer/agent@latest session new vwoNWCIAhOAVyz4RfKbR
```

That prints a session id; pass it to every later call as `-s <id>`.

## The commands

```bash
pnpm dev      # next dev, http://localhost:3000
pnpm framer   # design  → regenerates framer/, then re-applies the CMS binder
pnpm cms      # content → regenerates lib/cms.json from the Framer CMS
```

`framer` and `cms` are independent; neither implies the other.

---

## Layout

```
app/                     route tree — server components: metadata, params, 404 status
  layout.tsx             root; imports globals.css, framer/styles.css, lenis css
  page.tsx               /            → components/routes/Home
  about|program|mentor|pricing|contact/page.tsx
  program/[slug]/page.tsx  + generateStaticParams over lib/cms.json
  mentor/[slug]/page.tsx
  legal-pages/[slug]/page.tsx
  not-found.tsx          Framer's 404 design, served with a real 404 status
components/
  Shell.tsx              'use client' — nav + footer + cursor + site behaviours
  breakpoints.ts         breakpoint → Framer variant maps
  routes/*.tsx           'use client' — the sections each route renders
  CustomCursor.tsx       pointer-trailing dot
  shared.tsx             NotFoundNotice for a slug missing from the CMS
lib/
  cms.ts                 types, lookups, hydrateEmbeds, colour/font tokens
  cms.json               **generated** by `pnpm cms`
  useSmoothScroll.ts     Lenis, matching Framer's Smooth Scroll component
  useCompactSections.ts  scales section padding to ⅔ of the template's
framer/                  **generated** by `pnpm framer`
scripts/                 bind-cms.mjs, export-cms.mjs, export-cms.framer.js
next.config.ts           reactStrictMode: false — required, see Gotchas
```

### Why the Framer tree is client-only

`Shell.tsx` gates the whole Framer tree on mount. Two reasons, both load-bearing:

1. unframer's font store **fetches `framerusercontent.com` when it renders on a
   server**, so `next build` cannot prerender any page from a machine that
   cannot reach Framer's CDN. That is a hard build failure, not a warning.
2. `WithFramerBreakpoints` server-renders *every* breakpoint variant, then
   strips the inactive ones from the DOM as soon as its module is evaluated in
   the browser — which happens **before** React hydrates. That DOM surgery is
   what a hydration mismatch is made of.

The Vite original was a pure client-side SPA, so this is parity, not a
regression. Routing, `metadata`, `generateStaticParams` and the 404 status still
come from the server; only the painted output is client-rendered.

If you ever need real SSR HTML, the blocker is (1) — it needs an unframer that
does not touch the network during server render.

### Routing

File-based. `Shell.tsx` wires Framer's internal links into `next/navigation`:
`UnframerProvider navigate={...}` handles links that go through unframer, and a
document-level click handler catches the ones that bypass it, with the usual
escapes (new tab, modifier-click, external, `mailto:`).

Route paths must match the table unframer generates (`routes` in
`framer/chunks/chunk-*.js`) — Framer's own links point at those exact paths.

### Breakpoints

`.Responsive` ships with `defaultResponsiveVariants = {}` — empty — so without
an explicit map nothing switches. `components/breakpoints.ts` passes:

```
base/sm → Phone     md/lg → Tablet     xl/2xl → Desktop
```

Navigation has its own map: `Phone - Close`, `Tablet - Close`, `Desktop`.

### Two CSS fixes in `app/globals.css`

```css
.unframer-page > * { width: 100% !important; }
.unframer-page    { overflow-x: clip; }
```

1. Framer authors each component at a fixed breakpoint width (1200/810/390), so
   the exported roots render at that width flush-left in a wider viewport. A
   published Framer site stretches the breakpoint frame; this reproduces that.
2. The curved ticker ribbon in the Home hero is deliberately wider than the
   viewport. `clip` not `hidden` — `hidden` would make this a scroll container
   and break `position: sticky` descendants.

## Getting components out of Framer

unframer exports **only components ticked in the React Export plugin** inside
Framer. Creating a component is not enough, and publishing does not help. There
is no API and no `--include` flag — it is a manual tick, then `pnpm framer`.

37 components are ticked. To check without opening Framer:

```bash
curl -s -H 'X-Agent: cli' \
  https://unframer.co/api/plugins/reactExportPlugin/project/136c9ca46c906301 \
  | python3 -c 'import json,sys; [print(c["name"]) for c in json.load(sys.stdin)["components"]]'
```

**When a section is missing from a page, check the ticked list first.** A
section that exists in Framer but is not ticked produces no file and no error —
the page just renders short.

---

## The CMS binding patch — read before touching `components/routes/`

unframer emits every CMS binding as a **module-level stub**:

```js
var QLObxbGfmK3J5jRO36 = void 0;   // <fieldId><pageId>
```

They are not props — the only prop these components expose is `variant`. They
are module-scoped `var`s though, so `scripts/bind-cms.mjs` appends a
`__bindCmsFields(values)` export to each affected file. The route components
call it **during render, immediately before** rendering:

```tsx
bindHero(fields)
return <Hero.Responsive variants={RESPONSIVE} />
```

That shared module state is a second reason those subtrees must not render on a
server: concurrent requests would write to the same vars.

Do **not** rebuild these pages by hand — the whole point is to keep Framer's
real layout.

### CMS rich text can contain components

A `formattedText` field does not have to hold text. Several here hold a
**component embed** instead, and the CMS plugin API has no HTML representation
for one, so it reports the cell as `{ type: "formattedText", value: "" }`. The
content is only visible on the collection **item node**, as
`$control__<field>: [{ type: "TextComponentInstance", ... }]`.

Embed-backed fields (46 cells): Program `Syllabus Part 01–04` → `Subject Card`,
Program `Session Type 01–03` → `Session Type Card`, Program `FAQs` →
`General Accordion`, Mentor `Expertise` → `Team Expertise`, Mentor
`Session 01–03` → `Session Card`.

Three rules, all load-bearing:

1. `export-cms.framer.js` reads the item node, not just `fieldData`.
2. **Empty-string props must be preserved.** Cards resolve a control as
   `listItem05 ?? props.C8oax9OnP ?? "Word problems"` then hide the row with
   `isSet()`. `""` means hidden; dropping the key shows a placeholder.
3. **`hydrateEmbeds` must return a single element.** unframer's `RichText` does
   `children: isValidElement(content) ? content : void 0` — an array is not a
   valid element, so multiple embeds need a `Fragment`.

Any component in `EMBED_COMPONENTS` must stay ticked or the import breaks the
build.

## Gotchas

- `lib/cms.json` is a **snapshot**. Content edited in Framer does not appear
  until `pnpm cms`.
- After `pnpm framer`, hard-reload before concluding anything is broken.
- **Four ways a block silently renders empty**, none of which log anything: the
  component is not ticked; its CMS field is an embed the export dropped; the
  bound value is an array where `RichText` wants a single element; or React
  Strict Mode defeated the appear effect (next bullet). Rule them out in that
  order.
- **`reactStrictMode: false` in `next.config.ts` is load-bearing.** Framer's
  appear-on-scroll effects are one-shot -- the generated components pass
  `__framer__animateOnce`. Strict Mode mounts everything twice in development:
  mount → effect → cleanup → mount. The cleanup returns the element to the
  effect's initial state (`opacity: 0`, `translateY(30px)`) while the
  "already animated" flag survives, so the second mount never replays it. Every
  section below the fold then stays invisible forever and the page reads as a
  hero and nothing else.

  What makes this one expensive to diagnose: **an element at `opacity: 0`
  occupies exactly the space a visible one does.** Page heights, section counts,
  the generated files, `cms.json` and the binder all compare byte-identical to
  the Vite version while the site looks broken. Measure *visibility*, not
  height. The scan that finds it:

  ```js
  [...document.querySelectorAll('*')].filter(e => {
      const r = e.getBoundingClientRect()
      return r.height > 80 && r.width > 80 && parseFloat(getComputedStyle(e).opacity) === 0
  })
  ```

  A stuck element reads `opacity: 0` with `transform: matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 30)`.
  The Vite version renders without StrictMode (a bare `createRoot().render`),
  which is why the same components animate correctly there. Development only --
  production builds do not double-invoke effects -- but that is where the site is
  looked at most.
- The Framer tree needs a browser that actually paints. A hidden or throttled
  tab runs **no `requestAnimationFrame` callbacks**, so appear effects and any
  RAF-driven animation stay frozen at their initial state even when the code is
  correct. Headless or background-tab checks will report a broken page that is
  fine; confirm animation behaviour in a real, visible window.
- Images are **not in this repo**. Every one is a hot-link to
  `framerusercontent.com`, so the site needs network to look right and dies if
  that Framer project is deleted.
- The `AGENTS.md` block is rewritten by `next dev`. Commit it with your work
  rather than fighting it.

## Known gaps

- **Site has never been published** — no production URL exists.
- The Vite original's dev page-switcher was not ported; use the URL bar.
